identity.title: Facial droop, arm drift, abnormal speech (Cincinnati/FAST screen)

technique.how: Ask the patient to smile or show teeth (look for asymmetric facial movement); hold both arms out palms-up with eyes closed for 10 s (look for one arm drifting down); repeat a simple sentence (listen for slurred or wrong words or inability to speak). Any one abnormal item is a positive screen.
technique.prerequisites: Patient awake enough to follow commands; check a fingerstick glucose alongside the screen.
technique.contraindications: None; do not delay stroke activation to complete the screen if a deficit is already obvious.

interpretation.positive_finding: Any of new facial paresis, arm drift, or abnormal speech: pooled LR about 5.5 for stroke, higher for anterior-circulation events.
interpretation.negative_finding: All three items normal lowers but does not exclude stroke (pooled LR about 0.4); posterior-circulation strokes presenting with dizziness or ataxia are frequently missed by this screen.
interpretation.pitfalls: Isolated lower-facial weakness with forehead sparing suggests central lesion, whereas whole-face weakness suggests Bell palsy; hypoglycemia and post-ictal (Todd) paresis mimic all three items. Pre-existing deficits and dysarthria from intoxication produce false positives.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: activate stroke pathway and get immediate neuroimaging plus glucose. Negative in a dizzy or ataxic patient: do NOT stop; proceed to gait and HINTS-type assessment.

estimates.target_condition: Acute stroke (ischemic or hemorrhagic), final diagnosis after neuroimaging
estimates.population: Adults with neurologically relevant symptoms evaluated for possible stroke (pooled from studies using modern neuroimaging)
estimates.reference_standard: Final clinical diagnosis after neuroimaging and relevant laboratory tests
estimates.quote: LR of > or =1 finding = 5.5; 95% CI, 3.3-9.1 ... LR of 0 findings = 0.39; 95% CI, 0.25-0.61
estimates.location: Abstract, Results (LR for >=1 of facial paresis, arm drift, abnormal speech vs 0 findings)

estimates.target_condition: Stroke or TIA (physician-scored CPSS, any 1 of 3 items abnormal)
estimates.population: Convenience sample of 171 ED and neurology inpatients, 49 with stroke/TIA
estimates.reference_standard: Final diagnosis of stroke or TIA (physician certified in NIH Stroke Scale scored the CPSS)
estimates.computed_from: LRs computed from abstract sens 0.66 and spec 0.87: LR+ = 0.66/(1-0.87) = 5.08; LR- = (1-0.66)/0.87 = 0.39. Prevalence = 49/171.
estimates.quote: Observation by the physician of an abnormality in any 1 of the 3 stroke scale items had a sensitivity of 66% and specificity of 87%

estimates.population: Same 171-patient ED/neurology-inpatient sample, anterior-circulation stroke subgroup
estimates.reference_standard: Final diagnosis of stroke with anterior-circulation localization
estimates.quote: The sensitivity was 88% for identification of patients with anterior circulation strokes.

sources.citation: Goldstein LB, Simel DL. Is this patient having a stroke? JAMA. 2005;293(19):2391-2402.
Kothari RU, Pancioli A, Liu T, Brott T, Broderick J. Cincinnati Prehospital Stroke Scale: reproducibility and validity. Ann Emerg Med. 1999;33(4):373-378.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use a negative screen to exclude posterior-circulation stroke in acute dizziness, ataxia, or isolated visual loss; sensitivity for those presentations is low.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Any positive item with acute onset is a time-critical stroke until proven otherwise; check glucose but do not wait for other workup before imaging and stroke-team activation.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Kothari 1999: prehospital-provider reproducibility ICC 0.89 for total score (arm weakness 0.91, speech 0.84, facial droop 0.75); Goldstein 2005: reliability of individual neurological findings ranges slight to almost perfect, improved by NIHSS-style standardization.

extraction_notes: Pooled LRs taken verbatim from the JAMA RCE abstract (PMID 15900010); the two LR fragments are joined with an ellipsis because the full sentence exceeds 25 words. Kothari 1999 numbers are from the abstract; the RCE prior probability of stroke (10%) is a pretest estimate, not a study prevalence, so prevalence is left null for the pooled entry. Full RCE table not accessible (JAMA not in PMC), so location is the abstract.
